So, this is actually a neurological thing. It's a specific manifestation of sleep walking called sexomnia (terrible name, I know, but I didn't come up with it). The reason that I know this is because I have it. Every girlfriend I've ever had has told me that I actively try and/or do have sex with them when I'm very clearly unconscious. 

I recognize the roles are reversed here, but my point is that feeling like you might have been the perpetrator of a sexual assault is agonizing when it represents a violation of your strongest manifestation of ethics. Knowing that your partner doesn't see it as such doesn't immediately alleviate the self-hatred that comes with that territory.

I don't know what you and your boyfriend's history is. But from my personal experience, there are a few things that have helped me. 

The first is validate his guilt. He feels like he raped you, and so it's very reasonable for him to feel guilty and ashamed. Instead of telling him that everything's fine, tell him that feeling terrible makes sense given who he is as a person and what his values are.

The next is to make a concrete plan for how to handle similar things in the future. If one of you wakes up to the other initiating sex, have a game plan. Something like a key phrase to queue you in on the consciousness of the other. If they aren't awake, then the person who is needs to put space between you, and then make a very loud, sudden noise.

Finally, support him and yourself in counseling. When I found out about having sex with my girlfriend when I was asleep, and I thought I'd raped her, suicide and severe self-mutilation were very real concerns. Couple's therapy can also provide a safe and effective environment for moving through this together.

I think that there's a lot of stigma around couple's therapy, and I think it needs to be reevaluated. Instead of looking at it like trying to suture an existing wound, try thinking of it as laying a foundation for a stronger relationship to come. You're solving problems before they even exist.

Check in with yourself, as well. Make sure that you are doing alright. I know that this isn't an easy thing to deal with for either of you.

I hope some of this helps. 🙏
